sections.title: Interview bank U05: Quantization, sparsity, structured operators

keyTerms.definition: Original practice, role-derived material. Not actual lab questions.
A set of breadth, ladder, analytical, debug, scenario, and critique questions per unit.

recall.question: What is the provenance of this interview bank?
recall.answer: Original practice, role-derived. The questions are not actual lab questions.

keyTerms.definition: The integer level for 0.0: z = round(-min/s).
One (s,z) per row; survives skewed channel ranges.
Exactly 2 nonzeros per 4 consecutive elements.
Zero the smallest-|w| fraction; upgrades: sensitivity-guided, gradual + retrain.

recall.question: Write the four linear quantization formulas (s, z, x_q, x_hat).
Define per-tensor, per-channel, per-group quantization. When is per-tensor unsafe?
recall.answer: Per-tensor: one (s,z). Per-channel: one per row. Per-group: one per g elements. Per-tensor is unsafe when channels span very different ranges.

recall.question: Define 2:4 sparsity. Why does the pattern matter more than the sparsity count?
recall.answer: Exactly 2 nonzeros per 4 consecutive elements. The pattern matters because hardware skips only supported patterns; unstructured pays index overhead.

keyTerms.definition: In-range error: nearest mark is at most half a spacing away.
Sweep clip percentile; total MSE is U-shaped; the argmin is the pick.

recall.question: Deep ladder 1 works quantization on range [-1,1], 4 bits. What are s, z, and the round-trip of 0.5?
recall.answer: s=0.1333, z=8, x_q=12, x_hat=0.5333. In-range error bounded by s/2.

keyTerms.definition: Measured time; the FLOP ratio ignores index/gather overhead.
What eats the math saving: 45 us turns 2x math into ~1x.
2:4 needs sparse tensor cores; without them it runs as dense.

recall.question: Deep ladder 2 asks when 50% unstructured sparsity gives ~1x despite halved FLOPs. When?
recall.answer: When gather overhead eats the math saving: 50 us math + 45 us gather = 95 us ~ 1x. Realized time is what matters, not the FLOP ratio.

keyTerms.definition: The [-1,1] channel crushed by the [-100,100] scale under per-tensor.
~225x worse under per-tensor than per-channel on the toy.
Early-layer error gets multiplied by later Lipschitz constants.

recall.question: W has rows in [-100,100] and [-1,1], 4-bit. Compare the quiet channel’s MSE under per-tensor vs per-channel.
recall.answer: Per-tensor s=13.33: quiet channel MSE ~0.333. Per-channel s=0.1333: MSE ~0.00148. Ratio ~225x.

recall.question: Two layers, per-layer error 0.02, Lipschitz [1.0, 2.0] vs swapped. Which layer keeps more precision?
recall.answer: Order [1.0,2.0]: bound 0.06. Swapped: 0.04. Keep more precision early when later layers amplify.

keyTerms.definition: The bug: z = 0 hardcoded instead of round(-min/s).
dq(q(0.0)) == 0.0 exactly.

recall.question: D1. The quantizer looks right but quantize(0) does not decode to 0. What is the bug, the fix, and the invariant?
recall.answer: Bug: z = 0 hardcoded. With min != 0 the true zero point is round(-min/s) != 0. Fix: compute z from the range. Invariant: dq(q(0.0)) == 0.0 exactly.

keyTerms.definition: Optimal granularity would be per-element; metadata ratio is the limit.
No approximate method meets it literally; int8 + proof, or reframe.
Practical optimum with small g, bounded by scale overhead.

recall.question: Scales are free (zero storage, zero compute). What is the optimal quantization granularity now, and what limits it?
recall.answer: Per-element scales would be optimal (exact ranges), but scale storage then equals data storage. Practical optimum: per-group with small g.

recall.question: The error budget is zero but memory must halve. Compare int8, 2:4 sparsity, butterfly. Which do you pick?
recall.answer: int8 and 2:4 are approximate (fail the zero budget strictly); butterfly is exact only if representable (rare). Honest answer: no method meets both; nearest is int8 with task deltas zero within eval noise.

keyTerms.definition: Which tasks? Perplexity-only invalidates.
One run invalidates; demand seeds and error bars.

recall.question: A paper claims “4-bit weights with no quality loss on all tasks.” What five audit questions do you ask?
recall.answer: (1) Which tasks? (2) Baseline tuned? (3) Granularity and calibration reported? (4) Seeds and error bars? (5) Outlier-sensitive tasks included?
